title: QUIZ - 89
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table of input-output pairs shows a linear or nonlinear pattern
questions.question: Does the relationship shown in {(1, 3), (2, 12), (3, 27), (4, 48)} represent a linear or nonlinear pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: Nonlinear, because all the outputs are positive.

options.label: B
options.text: Nonlinear, because the differences between consecutive outputs are not constant.

options.label: C
options.text: Linear, because the differences between consecutive outputs are constant.

options.label: D
options.text: Linear, because the inputs increase by 1 each time.

questions.explanation: The differences between consecutive outputs are [9, 15, 21]. These differences are not constant, so the relationship is nonlinear.
questions.hint: Check whether the differences between consecutive outputs (for evenly spaced inputs) stay the same.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that a quadratic, exponential, or inverse formula produces a nonlinear relationship
questions.question: For the relationship \( y = 2^x \), is the rate of change between consecutive x-values constant?

options.label: A
options.text: The rate of change is always exactly zero.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, the rate of change is constant, so this is a linear relationship.

options.label: C
options.text: No, the rate of change is not constant, so this is a nonlinear relationship.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only when x is a whole number.

questions.explanation: For \( y = 2^x \), computing outputs at consecutive x-values shows changing differences between them, confirming this relationship is nonlinear.
questions.hint: Compute the outputs for a few consecutive x-values and check whether their differences stay the same.
